text.paragraph: New-patient primary care visit for counting, washing, and food rituals that are taking hours each day, with weight loss and sore hands. Concerns: Counting, calculating, and repeating everything in threes now takes hours each day and is slowing his work just when his largest project needs him; Fear of dirt and germs: he washes his hands dozens of times a day until they crack, wipes cutlery before he eats, and avoids shaking hands; Meals take so long to calculate that he skips them, and he has lost weight; he sleeps about four hours a night. [S]

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Structured assessment: Y-BOCS symptom checklist and severity scale, PHQ-9, GAD-7, and AUDIT-C today; interview for tics, bipolar disorder, psychosis, hoarding, and body dysmorphic symptoms; thyroid, blood count, metabolic panel, albumin, and vitamin B12 for weight loss
Psychiatry consultation to confirm the diagnosis, review comorbidity, and advise on sertraline dosing and the length of the trial

Exposure and response prevention with the clinic psychologist, weekly for 16 to 20 sessions, with a hierarchy he builds himself (touching door handles, shaking hands, eating without calculating, doing things in numbers other than three) and homework between sessions

Start sertraline 50 mg each morning; if the response is inadequate after four to six weeks, raise it in 50 mg steps every four to six weeks as tolerated, up to 200 mg, warning him about side effects and checking for them after each increase; judge the response only after eight to twelve weeks with at least four to six weeks at the top tolerated dose; continue for one to two years after a response
Collaborative safety plan with warning signs, coping steps, people to contact, the clinic number, and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline; suicide-risk review at every visit

Nutrition: three fixed mealtimes, energy-dense foods he accepts, a session with the clinic dietitian, and weight at every visit; eating without calculating is an exposure target, not a rule imposed at the table
Hands: petrolatum after each wash and at night, cotton gloves overnight, nitrile gloves for laboratory solvents; cutting down washing is part of the exposure work
Sleep: a fixed six-to-seven-hour sleep window, no laboratory work after midnight, and a sleep diary

Respectful examination: explain each step and ask before touching; offer hand sanitizer, gloves, and paper covers before and after; let him wash if he wishes; no handshake expected; no unplanned exposures in clinic, which belong in therapy
Y-BOCS down by at least 35 percent (treatment response) by twenty-four weeks
Y-BOCS 13 at twenty-four weeks, down 54 percent from 28

Rituals about 45 minutes a day; most meals eaten without calculation
BMI at least 18.5 with three meals a day
Hands healed, with washing under 15 times a day
Skin healed; washing about 12 times a day by twelve weeks
At least six hours of sleep most nights

list.item: At intake, rituals take three to four hours a day; meals take up to an hour because he calculates the volume of each portion, so he often skips them; he avoids handshakes in investor meetings; laboratory work slows because he repeats steps until they come out in threes [S]
Very tall and thin, immaculately dressed; formal, precise, and articulate; declines a handshake courteously and asks to use his own pen [S]

Mood "wound tight"; affect anxious and reactive; thought process linear and detailed; obsessions about contamination and numbers that he recognizes as excessive (good insight); describes vivid deliberate visual imagery of his designs that he knows is his own imagination; no hallucinations or delusions; no suicidal ideation, intent, or plan; judgment good [S]

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 1902-01-13: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent. Outpatient care with a collaborative safety plan, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, and a two-week follow-up [S]
